classification.habit: Twining annual or short-lived perennial climber
classification.habitat: Warm open woodland, field margins and tropical cultivated areas
classification.distribution: Widely distributed in tropical regions and cultivated in India

identification.description: A vigorous climber with trifoliate leaves, purple to white flowers and curved pods densely covered by irritating hairs.
identification.whole_plant: Twining climber capable of covering shrubs and supports.
identification.root: Strong root system; not a primary field character.
identification.leaf: Trifoliate leaves with ovate to rhomboid leaflets.
identification.flower: Papilionaceous flowers in hanging racemes, commonly purple, violet or white depending on variety.
identification.fruit: Curved or sickle-shaped pod densely covered with stiff irritating hairs.
identification.seed: Large hard seeds, usually dark or mottled, enclosed in the hairy pod.
identification.bark: Not applicable as a distinct medicinal bark character.

dosha.pitta: not specifically documented in imported dataset

major_constituents: Other seed proteins and phenolic/secondary metabolites
phytochemistry.chemical_notes: Mucuna pruriens seeds are a known natural source of L-DOPA. Content varies with variety and processing; medicinal preparations should not be dosed from raw-seed concentration assumptions.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Mucuna pruriens is studied particularly because its seeds contain L-DOPA. This does not establish that all traditional preparations are clinically interchangeable with standardized medicines.
modern_information.safety_notes: Seed hairs can cause marked skin irritation. Use authenticated, appropriately processed material and specialist guidance for therapeutic preparations.

student.quick_revision: Kapikachhu is a Mucuna climber with trifoliate leaves and irritating hairy pods; seeds contain L-DOPA.

teaching_points: Demonstrate Fabaceae papilionaceous flower and pod morphology.
Explain the difference between raw seed, processed drug and standardized L-DOPA.
discussion_points: Traditional Vrishya/Medhya descriptions versus modern pharmacology
practical_points: Do not handle hairy pods with bare skin.
Observe trifoliate leaf and pod morphology from a safe specimen.

key_precautions: L-DOPA content makes preparation-specific safety and interaction review important.
